What the numbers say

For the session of Thursday, November 19, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (36 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as risk-off. SPY is below its 50-day average and below its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

4 of 36 tickers (11%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 10 of 34 (29%) above their 200-day average. Below 30% is the level the model treats as weak breadth, which is enough on its own for a risk-off reading. On the day 4 rose and 32 fell; the median move was −2.69%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Technology had the strongest average move at −2.36% and Healthcare the weakest at −4.40%, a spread of 2.04 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.54 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

6 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (NVDA, BABA, UNH, IREN, SNDK, GOOG), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-18), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 25% to 11%, and the regime reading stayed risk-off.
